samples.summary: CLI image fetcher snapshots the JWT once and never refreshes on 401, so workspace-scoped images are silently dropped from an export when the access token expires
samples.evidence: `authorization: authorizationHeader(getConfig(opts))` captures the header value once, before the export runs. `HttpClient.refreshSession()` (packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:246) is the only place a stale `accessToken` is renewed, and the fetcher has no equivalent: a 401 from `GET /api/v1/workspaces/:wid/images/:id` becomes `httpError(401)` in `createImageFetcher`, which `pdf-export.ts:118` / `docx-export.ts:41` / `pptx-export.ts:22` funnel into `reportSkippedImage`. The image is dropped from the document with only a stderr warning — the exact failure mode this change exists to fix — whenever the session's access token is past `expiresAt` (config.ts:71 documents that it may be) and no earlier request happened to refresh it, or when expiry is crossed mid-export of a large document.

samples.summary: Shared-constant docs still say there are exactly two upload routes; this change adds a third
samples.evidence: `MAX_IMAGE_UPLOAD_BYTES`'s comment says "both upload routes (`POST /images` and `POST /api/v1/workspaces/:wid/images`)", `IMAGE_UPLOAD_MULTER_LIMIT_BYTES` says "both upload routes", and `unsupportedFileTypeMessage` says "Four call sites produce it: the `fileFilter` on each of the two upload routes..." (line 54). `ApiV1ShareImageUploadController` is now a third `fileFilter` consumer of all three, and `image.constants.spec.ts:28` repeats the stale "Two upload routes" count. The invariant still holds (the new route calls the shared function rather than spelling the literal, so the source-scan test stays green); only the stated arithmetic is now wrong.

samples.summary: `setImageUrlResolver` does not invalidate `imageCache`, so entries keyed by a previous resolver's output are retained for the process lifetime
samples.evidence: `imageCache`/`pendingImageCallbacks` are keyed by `urlResolver(logicalSrc)`, and `setImageUrlResolver` (including the `install(null)` cleanup in `shared-document.tsx:913`) swaps the resolver without clearing either map. Nothing renders a wrong image — a changed resolver produces a different key and simply refetches — but the tokened entries from a shared mount are unreachable garbage that is never evicted, and a `naturalWidth === 0` failed element cached under one key is never retried even after the resolver that would fix it is installed. Same shape as the pre-existing slides/notes/sheets seams, so this is consistency drift rather than a new defect.
